verses.text: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron in Egypt. He said,
"This month is to be the beginning of months for you. It will be the first month of your year.
Tell the whole community of Israel that on the tenth day of this month, each man must take a lamb for his family, one lamb for each household.

If a household is too small to eat a whole lamb, they must share one with their nearest neighbour, according to the number of people. Work out how much lamb is needed by how much each person will eat.
The animal you choose must be a one-year-old male without anything wrong with it. You may take it from the sheep or from the goats.
Take care of it until the fourteenth day of this month. Then all the people of the community of Israel must kill their animals at sunset.
They must take some of the blood and put it on the sides and the top of the door frames of the houses where they eat the lambs.
That same night they must eat the meat roasted over the fire, along with bitter herbs and bread made without yeast.
Do not eat the meat raw or boiled in water. Roast the whole animal over the fire, its head, legs, and insides.
Do not leave any of it until morning. If any is left until morning, you must burn it.
This is how you must eat it: with your belt tied, your sandals on your feet, and your walking stick in your hand. Eat it quickly. It is the LORD's Passover.
On that same night I will pass through Egypt and strike down every firstborn, both people and animals. I will bring judgment on all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
The blood on your houses will be a sign for you. When I see the blood, I will pass over you. No deadly plague will touch you when I strike Egypt.
This day is to be a day for you to remember. For all time to come, you must celebrate it as a feast to the LORD. This is a law that will last forever.

For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. On the first day remove the yeast from your houses. Anyone who eats bread made with yeast from the first day to the seventh day must be cut off from Israel.
On the first day hold a holy meeting, and another one on the seventh day. Do no work at all on those days, except to prepare food for everyone to eat. That is all you may do.
Celebrate the Feast of Bread Without Yeast, because on this very day I brought your people out of Egypt, group by group. Celebrate this day for all time to come. It is a law that will last forever.
In the first month, eat bread made without yeast from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day.
For seven days no yeast may be found in your houses. Anyone who eats anything with yeast in it must be cut off from the community of Israel, whether he is a foreigner or born in the land.
Eat nothing made with yeast. Wherever you live, you must eat bread made without yeast."
Then Moses called all the leaders of Israel and said to them, "Go at once and choose lambs for your families, and kill the Passover lamb.
Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood in the bowl, and put some of the blood on the top and on both sides of the door frame. Not one of you may go out of the door of his house until morning.

When the LORD passes through to strike down the Egyptians, he will see the blood on the top and sides of the door frame. Then he will pass over that door, and he will not let the destroyer come into your houses to strike you down.
You and your children must obey these instructions as a law that lasts forever.
When you come into the land the LORD will give you, as he promised, keep this ceremony.
And when your children ask you, 'What does this ceremony mean?'

then tell them, 'It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD. He passed over the houses of the people of Israel in Egypt when he struck down the Egyptians, and he spared our homes.'" Then the people bowed down and worshipped.
The people of Israel did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.

At midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn son in Egypt, from the firstborn son of Pharaoh, who sat on the throne, to the firstborn son of the prisoner in the dungeon. He also killed the firstborn of all the animals.
Pharaoh, all his officials, and all the Egyptians got up during the night. There was loud crying in Egypt, because there was not a house without someone dead.
During the night Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, "Get up! Leave my people, you and the people of Israel! Go, worship the LORD, as you have asked.
Take your flocks and herds, as you said, and go. And bless me too!"
The Egyptians kept urging the people to hurry and leave the country. "If you do not," they said, "we will all die!"
So the people took their dough before the yeast was added. They wrapped their bread bowls in clothes and carried them on their shoulders.
The people of Israel did as Moses said. They asked the Egyptians for things made of silver and gold, and for clothes.
The LORD had made the Egyptians kind to the people, and they gave them what they asked for. So the Israelites took away the riches of the Egyptians.
The people of Israel travelled from Rameses to Succoth. There were about six hundred thousand men on foot, not counting the children.
Many other people went with them, as well as large flocks and herds of animals.
They baked flat loaves from the dough they had brought out of Egypt. The dough had no yeast, because they had been driven out of Egypt and had no time to make food ready for themselves.
The people of Israel had lived in Egypt for four hundred and thirty years.
At the end of the four hundred and thirty years, to the very day, all the LORD's people left Egypt like an army.
The LORD kept watch that night to bring them out of Egypt. So on this night all the people of Israel must keep watch to honour the LORD, for all time to come.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "These are the rules for the Passover: No foreigner may eat it.
But any slave you have bought may eat it after you have circumcised him.
A foreigner living with you for a while, or a hired worker, may not eat it.
It must be eaten inside one house. Do not take any of the meat outside the house. Do not break any of its bones.
The whole community of Israel must celebrate it.

If a foreigner living among you wants to celebrate the LORD's Passover, all the males in his household must be circumcised. Then he may take part like someone born in the land. But no man who is not circumcised may eat it.
The same law applies to the person born in the land and to the foreigner living among you."
All the people of Israel did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
And on that very day the LORD brought the people of Israel out of Egypt, group by group, like an army.
